claim: Expert raters agree only weakly on how novel an idea or product is; single-item agreement is near chance to moderate.
agent_test: Have 2 independent judge samples rate our agent's ideas; report split-half agreement against the 56% human baseline before trusting any novelty score.

claim: Pooling many expert raters turns weak single-rater agreement into good reliability (alpha .8-.96; aggregated pass count r .69 vs kappa .41 per test).
agent_test: Aggregate k cheap judge samples or tests by code (pass counts) and measure reliability gain per token versus one long judgment.

claim: The Consensual Assessment Technique works with domain experts but not with novices: nonexpert ratings were unreliable and correlated only .21 with experts, and crowd raters inverted the quality ground truth for poems; rater background shifts ratings.
agent_test: Treat a judge with no domain grounding as a novice rater: calibrate it against a small expert-labelled set per task class before use.

claim: Pre-execution novelty or excitement ratings do not predict post-execution outcomes; the LLM novelty lead at idea stage vanished or reversed after 43 experts executed the ideas.
agent_test: On tasks with a runnable check, compare judge-rank of ideas with pass rate after running; keep only judges whose rank correlates with run outcome.

claim: LLM judges ranking ideas or novelty levels without retrieval are at or near chance and below human-human agreement (50-53% vs 56%; macro-F1 17%; kappa about 0 on TTCW tests). New: on a controlled set mined from reviews, six judges flipped verdicts under prompt edits and went below chance for some backbones (d02), and 12 frontier LLMs approved 74% of proposals reviewers rated unsound (d13).
agent_test: Never let the agent's own judgment pick the final idea; compare a judge-pick to a random pick on our open-mode tasks at equal tokens.

claim: LLM judges and automatic scorers overrate machine-written text and model-generated ideas versus humans or experts (novelty mirage; AI stories rated 5.00; own-response originality falls 1.43 points when elaboration is removed). Boundary: one study found no self-preference or verbosity bias with a rubric plus run history. Gap search: the judge in the machine-story study did not write the stories, so that result is a machine-text preference, not own-output preference (d08). With style removed and authorship hidden, raw self-preference vanished after controls (S +0.003, d06), but authorship labels alone moved scores (d06) and own-output bias persisted for objective rubrics (more than 50% more likely to wrongly pass, d10). Self-preference seems to need recognizable style or a label.
agent_test: Strip authorship and length (score core idea only) before judging; test whether judge win-rate for the agent's output falls when length is equalised.

claim: Pairwise or comparative judging has no consistent advantage: it worsened the novelty bias in RQ-Bench and was below direct scoring for GPT-4o, but forced-choice ranking in small batches (15 items) lifted LLMs to rho .87 on poems.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare direct score, pairwise and batch-of-15 ranking for our selector against a run-based ground truth.

claim: Judges that retrieve prior work, or get a rubric plus run history, agree with humans better than bare judges, reaching about human-human level but only moderate (rho .36-.43, .50-.52, .73; kappa .59 on 32 items). Gap search: retrieval gains were at most 16 points, only for some judges, and retrieval sometimes made judges call ideas novel only because none of five retrieved papers covered them (d02, d04); a 'rubric plus run history' judge reached rho .73 against human annotation but was never checked against later outcomes (d09).
agent_test: Add retrieval of nearest prior solutions to the novelty check in open mode; measure rho to a held-out expert rating versus a bare judge.

claim: Embedding semantic distance tracks human originality at the latent level on the Alternate Uses Task (r .75-.91) but is weak at item level or in other tasks (S-DAT r .13-.24); trained scorers do better (r up to .81) and transfer imperfectly.
agent_test: Use embedding distance only for dedup and coverage; check its correlation with run-based quality on our tasks before using as a score.

claim: Automatic originality and quality scores are confounded by response length and elaboration (longer answers score higher; 65% of chosen stories were longer).
agent_test: Report every judge score residualised on length; compare ranks with and without it.

claim: Counting functionally distinct answers (classifier or semantic entropy) is a validated novelty-as-diversity measure: 79% agreement with human pairs, kappa .56 to human labels, and n-gram metrics diverge from humans.
agent_test: Log distinct_k of an open-mode draw set by code; use it as the stopping or restart signal instead of judge opinion.

claim: A single model's sample pool collapses to near-duplicates: about 5% of 4000 ideas remained after dedup at cosine 0.8; frontier models give few distinct answers; showing the model its earlier outputs restores diversity.
agent_test: Measure unique-idea yield versus draws with and without in-context history of earlier ideas at equal tokens.

claim: Novelty and usefulness are decoupled: reviewer overall score tracks novelty but novelty is uncorrelated with feasibility, and in agent runs more novelty did not give better impact.
agent_test: Score novelty and test-pass separately and select on the check; do not add them into one number.

claim: Asking a model to pick its own most creative candidate did not beat chance: the pick matched the diversity pick 29% vs 35.3% random; the agent's ranker and expert rerank overlapped on only 17 of 49 ideas.
agent_test: Compare self-judge top-k with random top-k on run outcomes.

claim: Task-specific trained scorers or reward models beat zero-shot LLM judges (poly-encoder r .74 vs GPT-4 zero-shot .2-.67; story preference 78% vs 73%).
agent_test: Not a scaffold element for us (no training); useful only as a reason to distrust zero-shot judging.

claim: LLM judges compress scores toward the middle (Gemma gave 3 about 80% of the time; models say medium novelty even against their own reasoning).
agent_test: Convert judge scores to ranks within the batch by code.

claim: Judge explanation text is often useful or close to expert rationale even when its score is poor.
agent_test: Use explanations only as hints for revision, never as evidence of correctness.

claim: Formal evaluation frameworks (Ritchie criteria, SPECS) give checklists of typicality, value and 14 creativity components but were validated only by builder opinion and re-interpreted by users; none was tested against downstream success. Gap search found no study that compares multi-criterion scores with pass/fail on a checkable task (gap 9 stays open; ALPS shows only the verification side, d18).
agent_test: Not adopted; use only as vocabulary. Our check is execution.

claim: Novelty is reference- and time-dependent: a project loses novelty as similar ones appear, and novelty judgments depend on which prior set is retrieved. Gap search: judge verdicts moved with the retrieved set and with a per-case date cutoff (d02, d03, d04); a time-split with a fixed cutoff gives an outcome-based novelty check (d01). No study varied the corpus date on the same ideas and measured the drift directly.
agent_test: Keep a per-run archive of produced ideas and score novelty against it plus retrieved priors.

claim: An LLM judge's novelty score for generated research ideas was negatively related to later materialization: Spearman -0.29 with matching real papers published in the next 30 months, and the judge could not separate a retrieval-grounded generator from a plain one that the outcome measure separated 2.5 to 1.
agent_test: Do not select the highest-novelty candidate by judge score alone; where earlier history exists, test judge scores against later matches.

claim: LLM novelty verdicts are unstable under plausible prompt changes: deleting one sentence changed gpt-5.4's verdict on at least 52.6% of pairs and swung accuracy 52.6 points; changes flip a quarter to a third of verdicts when ranking two ideation systems; a configuration validated on one judge or one data type does not transfer. Cheap prompted judges beat costly dedicated novelty pipelines.
agent_test: Run each judgment under 2 paraphrased prompts and treat disagreement as 'cannot tell'; never validate on human-written ideas only.

claim: Self-preference of a judge for its own model's output is small to absent under blind, style-neutral conditions for judging ideas or selections (S +0.003, GPT-5 not inflating own runs), but present for objective rubric items (more than 50% more likely to wrongly pass own output) and induced by authorship labels. Evidence conflicts because tasks, style visibility and the reference judge differ.
agent_test: Strip authorship and normalize style before judging; use a different model family as judge than the generator; never label an idea as the judge's own.

claim: Small pooling of judge calls helps a little and costs little: a 3-call vote adds a few points for pointwise novelty judging and up to 11 points for pairwise judging; pooling several different judge models cuts but does not remove self-preference. Longer reasoning on one call and extra retrieval gave at most 7 and 16 points. No study gives the k curve or an equal-token comparison.
agent_test: Use k=3 independent cheap judge calls with ties allowed instead of one long call; measure agreement at k=1,3,5 on our own rated set before changing k.

claim: A two-stage judge that first extracts evidence per rubric item and then scores it reached QWK 0.64 with experts on a multi-step creativity task, against about 0.2 to 0.25 for chain, tree or graph reasoning and 0.47 for fine-tuning on about 140 labelled samples; it also lowered the length-score correlation. A small labelled set is not enough to train a judge but a decomposed rubric needs none.
agent_test: Judge by extracting quoted evidence per criterion first, then scoring from the evidence only; keep length as a reported covariate.

claim: LLM judges inflate approval of research ideas and proposals, not only research questions: 12 frontier models approved 74% of proposals reviewers rated unsound (65% against expert labels), and prompt changes traded false approvals for false rejections; a literature-grounded evaluator still approved 65.7% of unsound ones.
agent_test: Treat an uncalibrated 'good idea' verdict as a weak prior; require a rated calibration set and a threshold chosen on it.

claim: Source-bounded novelty can be fixed by an explicit step that checks each claim against named evidence: telling judges to test narrowness moved them to experts (RQ-Bench), and claim-by-claim attribution repaired 72.2% of unsupported novelty claims against 39.1% for retrieve-and-revise and 11.7% for self-revision. Handing over the prior alone did not fix it (61 of 175 correct attributions). Both fixes were designed after seeing the failure.
agent_test: Add a claim-attribution check: for each novelty claim, name the nearest prior and what is left over; code checks the leftover is non-empty.

claim: In one small test, training for set-level diversity of research ideas did not lower the share of idea sets for which a coding agent got a supports verdict (success@3 33% vs 27%), while LLM-rated distance agreed with humans about as well as two humans agree (0.37 vs 0.36). No study shows that distinct-answer count or semantic entropy predicts which single idea is useful.
agent_test: Keep k distinct candidates for execution; do not use distinctness to rank them.
